A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SLM/ESMDiff research. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A-H are readable and support comparison, including content relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original conformation-generation evaluations on BPTI, conformation-changing pairs and IDPs, plus runtime measurements, ablations and a nanobody inpainting case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds ESM3/ESMDiff evaluation on ATLAS MD ensembles in Appendix E.4 and Table S6.

M1.justification: The structure tokenizer, conditional language models, masked-diffusion objective and Algorithms 1-5 retain their procedures. Renaming Gibbs sampling to Iterative Decoding does not change Algorithm 3. Appendix B.4 explains existing fine-tuning choices rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Appendix E.4 adds evaluation on the ATLAS test set, extending coverage to multiple proteins with 100 ns MD ensembles. This is a limited extension within protein conformation generation; the original training data, BPTI, conformation-changing pairs, IDPs and nanobody scenario remain.

E2.justification: New Table S6 compares ESM3 and ESMDiff against AlphaFlow-MD. This adds an MD variant beyond the base PDB AlphaFlow model explicitly used in the earlier comparisons. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added ATLAS evaluation references an existing benchmark split and introduces RMSF correlations, RMWD, PCA Wasserstein distances and contact-agreement metrics. Existing evaluation protocols remain unchanged. Detailed ATLAS sampling and training settings are not supplied, limiting conclusions about its implementation.

E4.justification: The ranking, fine-tuning, temperature, sampling-step and reconstruction analyses retain their evidence, as do the gallery failure case and nanobody study. The nanobody study is relocated. ATLAS adds benchmark evaluation rather than a separate ablation or targeted robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests relative to the other. The nanobody runtime uncertainty, 5.3 +/- 0.3 seconds, already appears in v1. ATLAS performance statistics do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table S6 adds ATLAS results: pairwise RMSD correlation is 0.48 for AlphaFlow-MD, 0.08 for ESM3 and 0.18 for ESMDiff; RMWD is 2.61, 7.27 and 7.48, respectively. These establish an additional weak-performance setting. Tables 1-4, retained ablation values and existing plotted trends are unchanged.

T1.justification: The ELBO, diffusion definitions, assumptions and derivations are retained. The general discrete-diffusion exposition moves from v1 Section 4.1 to v2 Appendix G.1, with corresponding renumbering. Expanded explanation of decoder independence does not introduce a different assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same SLM framework, ESMDiff contribution, conformation-generation claims and 20-100x speedup claim. Promoting the existing nanobody example to the main text does not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E.4 adds a specific limitation and hypothesizes that discrete tokens struggle with subtle motions in short MD trajectories. Appendix B.4 adds a rationale for matching masking to inference conditions. Section 5.2 explicitly discusses MSA advantages, and Section 6 adds side-chain, ligand and RNA extensions.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.5/Table S3 documents baseline training sources, cutoff dates and base models. Figure 5 adds parameter counts, and Appendix C explicitly specifies 25-step nanobody sampling. These are documentation additions, not established changes to retained experiments. The code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: The ATLAS discussion adds references to Vander Meersche et al. and MD-related work by Jing et al. and Lu et al.; the Dmitriev nanobody reference is removed. This modestly expands the MD research context while retaining the original positioning of SLM.

P1.justification: Focused reorganization moves general diffusion background to Appendix G.1 and the existing nanobody case study to Section 5.5. v2 standardizes Iterative Decoding terminology, expands several explanations and adds reproducibility and acknowledgments sections. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables S3 and S6, distinguishes overall-best from SLM-best scores using bold and underlining, expands the runtime legend and recolors the sampling-step curves. The nanobody figure moves from Figure S1 to Figure 6. Existing visual evidence is retained.

improvement.justification: The added ATLAS evidence and explicit failure interpretation make applicability clearer, while baseline metadata and broader best-score highlighting improve transparency. These are useful gains over v1 without changing the method or original benchmark results. Sparse ATLAS protocol details limit the strength of the additional evidence.
